title: NHS caterer Compass confirms plan to ditch main London listing for New York
summary: World’s largest catering group supplies big tech firms such as Microsoft, Google and Amazon in the US London’s stock market has been dealt a further blow as the catering company Compass Group confirmed plans to move its main listing to the US , saying it had become “a predominantly North American business”. The world’s largest catering group said the move would provide better access to “the world’s largest and deepest pool of capital,” as it kicked off a consultation with its shareholders, two-fifths of whom are based in the US. title: Tech sell-off resumes as Nvidia shares drop 5% and Anthropic tumbles below IPO price – as it happened
summary: Republicans and Democrats object over Trump’s role in Jensen Huang’s return as Nvidia CEO, following an affair with an alleged Chinese spy Democrats hit out at Nvidia and Trump over Huang’s return – US politics live Have you downloaded Meta’s AI assistant Muse or do you plan to? The AI doomsday threat: Distinguishing facts from fear Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia, despite concerns over his conduct and the supply of AI chips to China, may show that AI – and Huang himself – are ‘too big to fail’. That phrase was on everyone’s lips almost 20 years ago when the Global Financial Crisis struck, and several major banks were bailed out. Given Nvidia’s pivotal role in the AI capex rollout, the implications of Huang’s reinstatement could be profound. Borrowing from the GFC, are some technology CEOs now so systemically important to the future of AI and US leadership in the latest technology revolution that they cannot be fired? Questions around the scale of financing required and future monetisation remain, and the dependence on Huang for the future success of AI may paradoxically heighten those concerns especially given Anthropic fell despite yesterday’s broad market rally. “We must investigate these actions. No president who has invested in a private company should be involved in their board decisions. Congress must come together in swift bipartisan action and demand answers immediately.” Continue reading...

title: Compass’s logic for US listing is flimsy but UK ministers need to wake up to Footsie flight risk | Nils Pratley
summary: The contract caterer switching to New York is a big hit to the London Stock Exchange but what is being done to discourage others from delisting? That’s gratitude, eh? Compass Group built its business, in part, on contracts to serve dinners in British schools and run catering operations in NHS hospitals. Now it plans to switch its primary stock market listing to New York in 2028. Compass is a bad one for the London market to lose. First, it is the 18th largest company in the FTSE 100 index and one of the few that is the biggest in the world in its market (contract catering, not just for the public sector but for thousands of corporate clients). Second, its reasons for joining the stateside listing rush feel flimsy – but also dangerous. Continue reading...

title: The next fight for democracy is in the states | Stacey Abrams
summary: Defend those being targeted, even when the threat has not reached your door Welcome back to How We Win , a Guardian opinion series with bold ideas for America’s political future. Today’s edition was written by Stacey Abrams , a voting rights activist, author, and former Georgia house minority leader. On 3 November, from Arizona to Georgia to Pennsylvania to Wisconsin, where a 16-year Republican majority fell, voters flipped at least 12 legislative chambers, the strongest statehouse showing for pro-democracy candidates since 2008. This did not happen by chance. Our democracy will be measured by what we protect, what we build and whom we refuse to leave behind. Continue reading...

title: Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia is elite impunity | Moira Donegan
summary: After the CEO was reinstated after Trump’s pressure campaign, it is abundantly clear: there are different rules for rich people There are different rules for rich people. If you or I acted the way that Jensen Huang has been accused of acting – allegedly berating and mistreating employees, sleeping with subordinates, and seeming to carry on a staggering number of extramarital affairs, including one with a woman identified by US intelligence as a likely Chinese spy who helped smuggle the company’s product to China – we probably would find ourselves out of work and out of favor for quite some time. But this is not so for Huang, the tech founder and close ally to Donald Trump who was recently ousted from Nvidia, the chip manufacturer he founded. On Monday, after a pressure campaign from Donald Trump, JD Vance and other members of the Trump administration, Huang was reinstated as CEO by the Nvidia board. title: $150 for photos of Melania looking like a waxwork? Will the Trumps ever run out of money-making ideas? | Arwa Mahdawi
summary: From the first lady’s Amazon documentary to Barron’s energy drink, the family is raking it in during Donald’s second term. And that includes the president Melania Trump is not a regular mom. She’s “a very cool mom”. We know this because she says so in her very cool new TV docuseries , which no one asked for, but which Amazon made anyway. I should clarify that Melania: The Series is not to be confused with Melania, the 104-minute-long $75m (£57m) movie Amazon released earlier this year. You know, the one an industry insider called “the most expensive documentary ever made that didn’t involve music licensing”. Various people insinuated nasty things about alleged corruption when that film came out, but I think it’s sweet how patriotic Amazon seems to be. While our cup may runneth over with Melania content, I have good news for first lady fans. We’ve been graced with even more Melania merch. At the weekend, Melania announced an “exclusive collection of digital photographs by internationally acclaimed photographer Ellen von Unwerth” to complement her new docuseries. For the non-refundable price of $150 (£115) you get one black-and-white digital image of the first lady sitting on a chair and one photo in which she is posing next to a clapperboard. According to Melania’s website, she and “Ms von Unwerth worked collaboratively during a two-day shoot to develop this visual narrative”. Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? title: Trump must act now to stop a three-way nuclear arms race | Edward J Markey
summary: After the president’s meeting with Putin and Xi, the US must take the lead in restoring arms control agreements Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping met last week in southern China, where Trump said they would “talk about nuclear weapons and denuclearization”. It was the first time the leaders of the world’s three largest nuclear powers had come together to discuss the future of nuclear weapons. That discussion was long overdue.
